reuse.why: Link rules go through one prepareBankAccountLink used by all six providers, and clearBankLink is extracted and reused by unlinkAccount; but Fintegra's link and download functions are copies of the Akahu ones instead of reusing shared code.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount (~70 lines) and downloadFintegraTransactions (~40 lines) are near-verbatim copies of linkAkahuAccount and downloadAkahuTransactions, adding to the tree's per-provider copy pattern rather than factoring it.

placement.why: Link guards live in accounts/app.ts, the download in accounts/sync.ts beside the other providers, and the server path in server-config.ts, matching the existing layering.

scope.why: Covers exactly the four steps; the desktop-client edits are limited to the type-required provider map entries.

maintainability.why: The link rules (one holder, closed accounts, takeover) are owned by one helper, which is good, but a sixth copy of the link body and a fifth copy of the download routine make any future change to linking or downloading a six-place edit.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every *-accounts-link function calls prepareBankAccountLink first; unlinkAccount uses clearBankLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The Fintegra link/download functions are open copies of the Akahu ones (same structure and names), not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: accounts/app.ts prepareBankAccountLink: gained replaceExistingLink (with the holder-unlink branch) and a general closed-account check; all six link functions, including the new Fintegra one, call it and none re-implements the checks.
